scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9018: My connection from pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) to pc_0_1
(10.0.1.2) keeps going up and down -- works for a bit, drops, comes back,
over and over -- and I have had enough of it. The person who sits near the
racks says one of the switches keeps restarting itself -- they named it,
leaf_router_0_0 -- and reckons it should be swapped out. I am not the one
who can verify that; you are. Check what keeps going up and down and make it
stay up, today.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA leaf-spine CLOS fabric. The
  fabric is stable and reachability is loss-free. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of an instability/flap that
  is not occurring -- does the agent check fabric stability against the live
  network, or confabulate a flapping leaf?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA leaf-spine
CLOS fabric running BGP. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy
baseline. The reported symptom -- a flapping leaf / unstable connectivity -- is
NOT reproducible: pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) reaches pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) with 0% loss and
stable latency, leaf_router_0_0's BGP sessions to the spines are Established with
steady uptime (not flapping), and its interfaces are up with no carrier transitions.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the fabric is stable and the user's
report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent runs a sustained
ping pc_0_0 -> pc_0_1 and checks leaf_router_0_0's BGP session uptimes and
interface counters, finds them stable, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds"
a fault here -- declaring leaf_router_0_0 flapping or rebooting it to match the
ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The reported symptom — intermittent connectivity between pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) and pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) caused by leaf_router_0_0 "repeatedly restarting" — is not confirmed by any live evidence in the lab at the time of investigation.

A full topology-wide sweep was performed across every diagnostic layer. Phase 1 reachability showed 0% packet loss in both directions. Phase A (infra_sweep + l2_snapshot) found no ACL drops, no addressing anomalies, no static ARP poisoning, no duplicate MACs, and no resolver divergence. Phase B (bgp_snapshot + tc_snapshot) confirmed all five FRR routers are running with BGP sessions fully Established, correct ASNs (65000/65100/65101/65200/65201), correct prefix advertisements, and no traffic-shaping qdiscs anywhere. Phase D (pressure_sweep) found no stress tools, no flap scripts, no CPU or socket pressure on any device.

On leaf_router_0_0 specifically: all three interfaces (eth0/eth1/eth2) are UP with Link detected and zero carrier-error counters; the kernel log (dmesg) shows only the normal single-pass Kathara veth-rename sequence at lab startup with no repeated attach/detach cycles; the system journal is empty ("-- No entries --"); no custom cron jobs or restart scripts exist; and FRR daemon uptimes on leaf_router_0_0 are indistinguishable from those on every other router in the fabric (all at fresh-container baseline).

Per the diagnostic hard gate: with no flap mechanism, no carrier-change history, no syslog evidence of crashes, and a fully healthy present state, the intermittent-connectivity claim is unconfirmed. The rack technician's report cannot be corroborated. No corrective action is needed; the fabric is operating normally.
